newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg says to buy Bass' Carlsberg-Tetley stake.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg says to buy Bass' Carlsberg-Tetley stake.

text.p: Danish brewer Carlsberg on Friday said it would buy British partner Bass' 50 percent holding in their Carlsberg-Tetley alliance for 110 million pounds ($183 million).
The announcment followed a British government ruling that blocked the planned Bass purchase of Carslberg's half of the joint venture but said Bass must sell its existing stake.
"Obviously we are disappointed with the decision announced by the UK President of the Board of Trade," Carlsberg International Managing Director Michael Iuul said in a statement.

But he said that Carlsberg had known that stiff monitoring of the British brewing industry by competition authorities meant that the deal might be blocked and had found areas of savings within Carlsberg-Tetley which could be implemented without Bass.
"The fundamental structural reorganisation to be implemented in Carlsberg-Tetley within the next few years will obviously involve expenses for the company," he said.
"However it should be taken into consideration that Carlsberg will be taking over a 50 percent interest in the company for 110 million pounds, which is substantially below the market value."
After the British ruling, Carlsberg's share dropped 19.1 crowns, to 346.00 but by 1310 GMT had regained some ground, to 350.41.

Carlsberg-Tetley Managing Director Ebbe Dinesen said that the company was naturally disappointed at the British decision but at the same time relieved that seven months of uncertainty while British monopoly watchdogs deliberated was over.
"Now we can get down to work and get on with business," he told Reuters.
